title: A Cosmological Sector for the E8 × ωE8 Octonionic Unification: Electroweak Emergence, Covariant Infrared Gravity and Cosmological Tests
content: The \(E_8 \times \omega E_8\) octonionic programme motivates the joint emergence of classical spacetime and localised matter at an electroweak-scale transition. We formulate a conditional cosmological framework using the preferred-foliation action of Blanchet and Marsat as an explicit effective candidate. Its stationary weak-field branch yields MOND, but nonstationary systems also require the foliation equation. Linearising about a flat homogeneous universe gives an additional initial-data mode whose effective density scales as the inverse cube of the scale factor. Removing that mode gives the GR linear equations for the stipulated matter; neither its selection nor a MOND switch at recombination follows from the action. We identify a tension between rapid Newtonian recovery and a sufficient stationary stability criterion, without treating that criterion as a complete stability test. A conditional thermal history gives \(\Delta N_{\text{eff}} = 0.194\) when three sterile species and a dark photon are relativistic. Matching an assumed relic density gives masses near \(37~\text{eV}\) and an accumulated free-streaming distance near \(17~\text{Mpc}\) today in a reference background. Entropy dilution lowers the temperature, not the maximum fermion occupation, so phase space does not exclude these relics from galaxies. On the branch with the GR linear equations a Boltzmann calculation fits the Planck 2018 spectra worse than \(\Lambda\)CDM by \(\Delta\chi^2 \simeq 10\), with lensing power half the \(\Lambda\)CDM value at \(L = 1000\) and linear \(\sigma_8 = 0.70\), so the observed growth must arise outside that branch. The proposed \(a_0\)–\(\Lambda\)–Jordan relation is reassessed as a vacuum-dependent numerical ansatz. Primordial correlations, scalar stability, the foliation mode, nonlinear structure and cluster lensing remain open tests. The construction does not yet establish an observationally viable cosmology.
